Fit a rainfall generator to a record

Source: R/synthetic_rain.R
fit_rain.Rd

Estimates a generator's parameters month by month from a rainfall record, so that synthetic_rain() produces rain that resembles it.

Usage

fit_rain(
  record,
  method = c("nsrp", "bartlett_lewis", "markov_gamma"),
  wet_threshold = NULL
)

Arguments

record

A data frame with a time column (time or dateTime) and rain in mm per step (rain or value), at a regular step; or an object from reach.io::read_silver().

method

nsrp, bartlett_lewis or markov_gamma.

wet_threshold

A day or interval counts as dry at or below this depth, mm. By default 0 for the pulse models, whose dry proportion is for exactly no rain, and 0.1 for the Markov chain.

Value

A parameter table as rain_parameters() returns, with the record's and the fitted statistics as attribute fit.

Details

  • Pulse models (nsrp, bartlett_lewis): the method of moments. For each calendar month the model's exact mean, variance, lag-1 autocorrelation and dry proportion (see rain_statistics()) are matched to the record's at two interval lengths: 1 and 24 hours for a record at an hourly step or finer, 24 and 72 hours for a daily record. The mean is matched exactly; the others by least squares on relative errors, from several starts.

  • Markov chain with gamma amounts: maximum likelihood. Transition probabilities from counts of consecutive valid days; gamma shape and scale from the wet-day totals.

A month with fewer than 60 valid days borrows the parameters of its neighbours. Fitting takes seconds for the Neyman-Scott model and a few minutes for Bartlett-Lewis, whose dry proportion needs a double integral.

The record may come straight from reach.io: fit_rain(reach.io::read_silver(root, "SS92F014", "P")) reads the dateTime and value columns of its readings.

Examples

# \donttest{
observed <- synthetic_rain("2000-01-01", years = 20, seed = 3, pet = NULL)
fitted <- fit_rain(observed, "nsrp")
round(fitted[1:3, ], 3)
#>   month lambda  beta    nu   eta   mux
#> 1     1  0.014 0.058 3.871 0.541 0.892
#> 2     2  0.029 0.199 1.296 0.412 0.979
#> 3     3  0.019 0.213 3.361 0.752 1.257
# }
